On the left side, three visible triangle areas are respectively [ALT]=9, [AEL]=3, [ELS]=2, and A,L,S are collinear, E,L,T are collinear. On the right side, three visible triangle areas are respectively [TCR]=5, [CDR]=4, [SRD]=8, and C,R,S are collinear, D,R,T are collinear. Then reason: On the left side, [AEL] and [ELS] use AL and LS on the same straight line AS as bases, and have the same height, so AL:LS=3:2. Also [AEL] and [ALT] use EL and LT on the same straight line ET as bases, and have the same height, so EL:LT=3:9=1:3. Therefore [LST]=[AEL]·(LS/AL)·(LT/EL)=3·(2/3)·3=6. Similarly on the right side, the corresponding triangle areas formed by the crossing line segments satisfy [TRS]=[TCR]·[SRD]/[CDR]=5·8/4=10. The gray quadrilateral P is composed of triangles LST and TRS, so P=6+10=16.

method.method_draft: Label the grey quadrilateral vertices as T = top apex, L = left grey vertex, S = bottom grey vertex on the base, and R = right grey vertex. Read from the diagram that A,L,S are collinear on the left slanted cut and E,L,T are collinear on the other left cut, with triangle areas [ALT]=9, [AEL]=3, [ELS]=2. Draw the diagonal TS inside the grey quadrilateral. On the left, use equal-altitude area ratios: from [AEL]:[ELS]=3:2 get AL:LS=3:2, and from [AEL]:[ALT]=3:9 get EL:LT=1:3. Hence [LST]=[AEL]*(LS/AL)*(LT/EL)=3*(2/3)*3=6. Similarly on the right, read C,R,S collinear and D,R,T collinear with [TCR]=5, [CDR]=4, [SRD]=8. Apply the same area-ratio argument to get [TRS]=[TCR]*[SRD]/[CDR]=5*8/4=10. Add the two triangles of the grey quadrilateral: P=[LST]+[TRS]=6+10=16.
